title: U.S. House · California's 18th Congressional District
area: Most of San Jose and surrounding Santa Clara County communities.

context.text: California redrew its congressional district lines for the 2026 elections under Proposition 50, a mid-decade redistricting measure voters approved in a November 2025 special election.
In the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, Zoe Lofgren won 54.9% of the vote (65,291 votes) and Shane Lewis won 29.3% (34,883 votes), advancing them both to the November general election.

candidates.name: Zoe Lofgren
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for California's 18th District (since 1995, under prior district numbers)

summary.text: Zoe Lofgren is the Democratic incumbent for California's 18th District, serving in the House since 1995. An immigration attorney and former Santa Clara County supervisor, she is the ranking member of the House Science, Space and Technology Committee and serves on the Judiciary Committee. Her House website highlights immigration policy, technology and digital rights, and health care.

background.text: Born in San Mateo, California; her House website describes her as a lifelong Bay Area resident and the daughter of a truck driver and a cafeteria cook who attended public schools. Graduated from Gunn High School in 1966.
Attended Stanford University on a California State Scholarship, graduating with a bachelor's degree in political science in 1970, then earned a J.D. from Santa Clara University School of Law in 1975.
Served on the staff of Rep. Don Edwards in his San Jose and Washington offices (1970-1978, per her House website).

Practiced and taught immigration law, including as a faculty member at Santa Clara University School of Law, and was a founder and first executive director of the nonprofit Community Housing Developers.
Elected to the San Jose-Evergreen Community College District board in 1979, and in 1980 to the Santa Clara County Board of Supervisors, where she served 14 years.
Elected to the U.S. House in 1994 after Edwards retired; represented the 16th District from 1995 to 2013 and the 18th since 2013.
Is ranking member of the House Science, Space and Technology Committee, serves on the Judiciary Committee, and is elected chair of the California Democratic Congressional Delegation.

Led Democrats on the House Immigration and Citizenship Subcommittee for eight consecutive sessions and, in the 116th Congress, led negotiations on the Farm Workforce Modernization Act; her House website also cites her work on patent, copyright, privacy and digital-rights issues, including opposition to the Stop Online Piracy Act.

priorities.text: Lists expanding access to quality, affordable health care as a driving priority, including support for the Affordable Care Act and efforts to move toward Medicare for All.
Lists top-to-bottom immigration reform as a priority, including a path to citizenship for Dreamers and Temporary Protected Status recipients and reform of high-skilled and agricultural visa programs.
Lists reducing greenhouse gas emissions and opposing new offshore oil and gas drilling off the California coast as environmental priorities.

positions.summary: Is an original cosponsor of an assault weapons ban and supports universal background checks for all commercial gun sales.
positions.quote: Zoe is an original cosponsor of the Assault Weapons Ban which would prohibit individuals and manufacturers from selling and obtaining semi-automatic rifles, pistols, and shotguns as well as high-capacity magazines.

positions.summary: Is a member of the Medicare for All Congressional Caucus and cosponsors multiple bills to expand Medicare, including the Medicare for All Act.
positions.quote: Zoe is a member of the Medicare for All Congressional Caucus and supports efforts to make health care more affordable for and accessible to everyone. She believes expanding Medicare to all Americans is a good way to accomplish that.

positions.summary: Has worked to block funding for new immigration detention facilities and backs a pathway to citizenship for Dreamers and TPS recipients rather than expanded enforcement.
positions.quote: As for my role in Congress, I'm doing all that I can to block funding for new detention facilities.

positions.summary: Supports reducing greenhouse gas emissions and efficiency standards, and opposes new offshore oil and gas drilling off the California coast.
positions.quote: Zoe strongly opposes new proposals to permit offshore drilling anywhere off the California coast and has fought efforts to weaken the moratorium that protects our coastal and marine treasures.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on the Judiciary (Courts, Intellectual Property, Artificial Intelligence, and the Internet; Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement; The Administrative State, Regulatory Reform, and Antitrust subcommittees) and the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology in the 119th Congress.

Led bipartisan negotiations on the Farm Workforce Modernization Act, providing a path to legal status for an estimated 1.5 million farmworkers and improving the H-2A visa program; it passed the House with bipartisan support in the 116th and 117th Congresses.
Shepherded House passage of the American Dream and Promise Act, putting Dreamers and TPS/DED recipients on a pathway to citizenship, in the 116th and 117th Congresses.

candidates.name: Shane Lewis
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2 top-two primary with 29.3% of the vote

summary.text: Shane Lewis is the Republican candidate for California's 18th District. A U.S. Marine Corps veteran, he is an R&D electrical test engineer in the medical device industry and a former small-business owner and church worship leader in San Jose. He advanced from the June 2026 top-two primary with 29.3% and previously ran for the Santa Clara County Board of Education in 2024.

background.text: Born in Tallahassee, Florida; attended Rickards High School.

Joined the U.S. Marine Corps a few months after high school, serving from 1990 to 1995; he says he earned two meritorious promotions and qualified as a paratrooper at Fort Benning, Georgia. His 2024 survey says he served in the airwing.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Liberty University (2018, per Ballotpedia); his 2024 survey describes it as a B.S. in political science, with an M.S. in political science pending thesis defense.

Has worked as an engineer, engineering technician and failure analyst; his 2024 survey describes a career of over 30 years in failure analysis, reliability and electrical engineering for commercial, military-contract and medical device companies. He is currently an R&D electrical test engineer for a medical device company, with prior R&D roles at Zeltiq, Thoratec, St. Jude Medical, Abbott and Procept-Biorobotics.
Previously ran a small business teaching piano, voice and guitar, and served as a worship leader and elder at a church in San Jose.
Ran for Santa Clara County Board of Education (Trustee Area 4) in November 2024, finishing third with 21.3% of the vote.
Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, receiving 29.3% to Lofgren's 54.9%; states that he and his wife have four children.

priorities.text: Names immigration reform as a top issue, saying he would combine 'Republican respect for law and order with Democratic love of liberty' and criticizing Rep. Lofgren for blocking border-security measures.
Calls for a simple, low flat tax on wages, reduced regulation, and tax breaks framed around a 'Make America Healthy Again' agenda.
Prioritizes water and energy policy for the district, including wildfire prevention, hydropower expansion, desalination, and dam safety.

positions.summary: Supports combining stronger border enforcement with reforms addressing migrant exploitation, criticizing the incumbent for blocking border-security measures.
Calls for a simple, low flat tax on wages rather than higher taxes, saying government's core purpose is not 'to control lives or raise taxes.'
positions.quote: Government's core purpose is to secure our unalienable rights and liberties — not to control lives or raise taxes.

positions.summary: Supports hydropower expansion and dam infrastructure alongside wildfire and watershed management, without addressing a broader fossil-fuel transition.

sources.title: United States House of Representatives elections in California, 2026

researchNotes: Zoe Lofgren has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; positions and priorities above are drawn from her official House issues pages (lofgren.house.gov/issues), checked 2026-09-25. Federal key votes and FEC totals for both candidates are added separately by script. Biography gaps: Lofgren's birth year is not stated in the sources loaded; Lewis's birth year is not given. Lewis's prior summary said this is his second run against Lofgren, which Ballotpedia does not support (his 2024 race was for county board), so it was removed.
